nations.name: Coharie Tribe
nations.lands: Harnett and Sampson Counties in southeastern North Carolina, where the Tribe locates its present community

facts.text: The Tribe's history locates the present Coharie population in North Carolina's Harnett and Sampson Counties.
facts.evidence: in the counties of Harnett and Sampson

facts.text: The Tribe's history dates a Coharie-funded subscription school for its children to 1859.
The Tribe's government page describes the Coharie Intra-Tribal Council as representing Harnett and Sampson Counties.
The Tribe's river page dates volunteer work on the Great Coharie River to 2015.

source.title: Great Coharie River Initiative/Coharie River Tours - Coharie Tribe

facts.evidence: Starting in 2015, volunteers have been working

nations.name: Haliwa-Saponi Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Meadows area at present-day Hollister, North Carolina; the Tribe locates its government there without defining territorial boundaries in this source

facts.text: The Tribe locates its government in present-day Hollister, North Carolina, in the area it calls the Meadows.
facts.evidence: what was previously known as the “Meadows”

facts.text: The Tribe's website describes eleven Tribal Councilors, including a Chief and Vice Chief, elected by its citizens.
facts.evidence: elected by the citizens of the Tribe

facts.text: The Tribal School's stated mission combines academics, technology and community involvement with American Indian culture.

source.title: Haliwa Saponi Tribal School: Quality Education - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

facts.evidence: with the integration of American Indian culture

facts.text: The Tribe describes Red Earth as a program for all ages to learn about Haliwa-Saponi history and cultural practices.

source.title: Cultural Classes - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

facts.evidence: citizens and community members of all ages
